presentingComplaint: Brought in by family with 2 days of acute confusion, an unwitnessed fall, and rapidly worsening breathlessness; cough was minimal and easily missed at triage.
history: Independent, community-dwelling retired schoolteacher. Family noticed him becoming increasingly muddled and off his food over 48 hours, culminating in a fall at home this morning with new drowsiness. He had a mild dry cough for 4 days that he dismissed as 'a chest cold'; there was little sputum, so the illness was initially attributed to a urinary or neurological cause. No recent hospitalisation, no antibiotics in the past 90 days, no aspiration event or dysphagia, no injection drug use. Background: type 2 diabetes on metformin, treated hypertension, ex-smoker (30 pack-years). No travel, no TB contact. Influenza-like illness circulating in the community.
examination: Toxic and drowsy, GCS 13 (E3V4M6), disoriented to time and place. Peripherally cool and mottled with prolonged capillary refill. Marked tachypnoea with accessory muscle use and central cyanosis. Chest: bronchial breathing and coarse crepitations over the right mid/lower zone with dullness, plus new crackles at the left base — bilateral, multilobar signs. No calf swelling, no cardiac murmur, JVP not raised, abdomen soft and non-tender.

labs.abg: pH 7.30, PaO2 52 mmHg on room air, PaCO2 34 mmHg, HCO3 16

imaging: Portable chest radiograph: dense right middle- and lower-lobe consolidation with air bronchograms plus patchy left basal consolidation — multilobar involvement. No large effusion, no cavitation. Bedside lung ultrasound: bilateral consolidation with dynamic air bronchograms, no B-line oedema pattern. CTPA (done to exclude PE given hypoxia/hypotension): no filling defect, confirms bilateral multilobar consolidation.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures drawn before antibiotics. Sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs with Gram-positive diplococci. Urinary pneumococcal antigen positive; Legionella urinary antigen negative. Respiratory viral PCR pending. Blood cultures at 24h: Streptococcus pneumoniae, penicillin-susceptible.
differentialDiagnoses: Severe community-acquired pneumonia with sepsis-induced hypotension (multilobar pneumococcal)
Non-severe CAP (excluded by CURB-65 5, PaO2:FiO2 <250, multilobar involvement and vasopressor need)
Aspiration pneumonia (no witnessed aspiration, dysphagia or dependent-segment/cavitary pattern)
Septic shock from non-pulmonary source (source clearly pulmonary on imaging and micro)
finalDiagnosis: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (multilobar penicillin-susceptible pneumococcal) with acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure and septic shock — an atypical, confusion-and-collapse presentation in an older diabetic with minimal cough.
citations: ATS/IDSA — Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia — 2019
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Pneumonia
Surviving Sepsis Campaign — Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock — 2021
stewardship: Meets ATS/IDSA 2019 major criteria for severe CAP (septic shock requiring vasopressors; also PaO2:FiO2 168, multilobar infiltrates, confusion, uraemia). No MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors identified, so standard severe-CAP empiric therapy: IV ceftriaxone plus IV azithromycin (beta-lactam + macrolide), started within 1 hour with cultures drawn first. Add oseltamivir pending influenza PCR during flu season. De-escalate to IV benzylpenicillin/amoxicillin once penicillin-susceptible S. pneumoniae confirmed; total 5-7 days if clinically stable and afebrile 48-72h.
contraindications: Macrolide QT prolongation — review ECG/QTc and concomitant QT-prolonging drugs before azithromycin
Avoid fluoroquinolone as the macrolide alternative if it would mask/delay diagnosis of concurrent TB
Renal dose adjustment and nephrotoxin avoidance given AKI (creatinine 2.2)
edgeCases: Minimal cough in an older diabetic can mask pneumonia — confusion and a fall were the presenting features
Hypotension here is sepsis-induced from a pulmonary source, not a primary cardiovascular event
If cavitation or MRSA/Pseudomonas risk factors emerge, broaden empiric cover accordingly
expectedMaiK: Recognise this as SEVERE CAP (not non-severe CAP or undifferentiated septic shock): multilobar consolidation on imaging with positive pneumococcal antigen/cultures, meeting ATS/IDSA major criteria (septic shock + respiratory failure). Start empiric ceftriaxone + azithromycin within 1 hour, resuscitate for septic shock, and escalate to ICU/organ support.

Any aspiration event, dysphagia or reduced consciousness preceding illness?
Baseline functional status, resuscitation wishes and ceiling of care?
expectedInvestigations: Serum lactate and arterial blood gas
regressionAssertions: Engine must return SEVERE_CAP as top diagnosis, not non-severe CAP.
Must flag ATS/IDSA major severity criteria (septic shock/vasopressor need and PaO2:FiO2 168, multilobar infiltrates).
Empiric regimen must be a beta-lactam PLUS a macrolide (or respiratory fluoroquinolone), not beta-lactam monotherapy.
Blood cultures and antibiotics within 1 hour must be recommended for septic shock.
Must not misattribute presentation to a primary neurological or urinary cause despite confusion and fall.
